title: Personas & system prompts
blurb: How instructions shape a model’s voice, focus and boundaries.

slides.title: One model, many personas
body: A persona is a set of instructions — often a hidden “system prompt” — placed at the start of the context.
It tells the model who to be, how to sound and what to focus on. The underlying model doesn’t change at all.

visual.caption: The system prompt sits in the context window ahead of your message.

items.label: System prompt
items.text: You are a friendly tutor for beginners. Keep answers short and use everyday examples.

items.label: Model reply
items.text: Think of tokens as puzzle pieces of text…

slides.title: Same question, different persona
body: Both answers draw on the same underlying knowledge.
Tone, length and vocabulary change because the instructions changed — nothing else.

cards.label: Persona: patient tutor
cards.text: Think of tokens as puzzle pieces of text. The model reads the pieces, not whole words.

cards.label: Persona: technical reviewer
cards.text: Tokens are sub-word units produced by the tokeniser and mapped to integer IDs in a fixed vocabulary.

slides.title: What a persona can and can’t do
body: Personas are powerful for shaping behaviour, but they’re instructions — not upgrades.

visual.caption: A persona steers the model; it doesn’t change what the model knows.

items.heading: Can: set tone and format
items.text: Friendly or formal, bullets or prose, brief or detailed.

items.heading: Can: set focus and limits
items.text: Stay on one topic, or decline certain kinds of request.

items.heading: Can’t: add knowledge
items.text: Calling it an “expert” doesn’t give it facts it never learned.

quiz.question: Where does a persona usually come from?
options: Instructions such as a system prompt at the start of the context
A separate model trained for each persona
quiz.explanation: Personas are mostly instructions placed in the context. The same model can play many roles.

quiz.question: Telling a model “You are a world-class lawyer” will…
options: Give it legal knowledge it didn’t have
Change its tone and focus, but not what it actually knows
quiz.explanation: A role can sharpen focus and style, but it can’t add facts the model never learned — so you still need to check its work.

quiz.question: Two apps use the same model but feel very different. Why?
options: They give it different instructions and context
One copy of the model is secretly smarter
One of them is always online
quiz.explanation: Different system prompts, documents and settings in the context make the same model behave very differently.
